stories.title: Human and LLM Facilitation in Collaborative Design Meetings: A Computational Behavioral Comparison
stories.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored as facilitators of group discussion and collaborative work, but the behavioral differences between LLM-generated and human facilitation remain insufficiently characterized.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: The Evidence Anchoring Boundary: Where Visual Interventions Matter and When They Help in Multimodal LLMs
stories.summary: Visual interventions provide a training-free way to reduce hallucinations in multimodal large language models. However, an intervention may have little leverage at some layers and may damage a correct answer even when it changes the output.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: AgentTune: A Unified Training Lifecycle for Tool-Using LLM Agents
stories.summary: Tool-using agents increasingly require a common substrate for building, training, evaluating, distilling, and maintaining agentic systems, yet existing tooling typically addresses these stages in isolation.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: OGPO: Offline Goal-conditioned Policy Optimization for Recoverable Vision-Language-Action Models
stories.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong promise in robotic manipulation, yet their post-training still predominantly relies on trajectory-level supervised imitation over robot demonstrations.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: What Should SFT Learn? Conditional Information Gain for Generalizable Post-Training
stories.summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) remains a widely used approach for post-training large language models, because fixed demonstrations can directly introduce desired reasoning strategies and behavioral patterns.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: SpireBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Strategic Play of Agentic Models with Slay the Spire
stories.summary: Agentic large language models now tackle complex tasks, yet strategic reasoning over long horizons is under-studied: most agentic benchmarks are short and episodic, and performance on long tasks is hard to dissect into stored knowledge, reasoning and luck.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
stories.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming direct users of the open web. As they take on increasingly complex and information-intensive tasks, effective web access is becoming a core capability for agentic problem solving.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: AudioTETRIS: Token Elimination via Transitional Importance Signals for Efficient Audio LLMs
stories.summary: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) achieve strong performance on speech-text tasks, but standard audio encoders produce hundreds of tokens for even short audio clips.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: Grounded-Dreamer: Robot Learning from World Model Synthetic Data with Physical Grounding
stories.summary: Scaling robot manipulation policies requires large amounts of diverse, action-labeled data, yet collecting such data in the real world remains expensive and difficult to scale.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
stories.summary: Training long-horizon language model agents requires assigning credit to intermediate decisions from sparse terminal feedback.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: AMLworld-Compact: Importance-Weighted Downsampling for Cost-Effective LLM Evaluation and Error Diagnosis
stories.summary: Evaluating large language models (LLMs) on AMLworld's smallest test splits is costly because each of over a million targets requires a separate graph prompt. Sampling reduces this cost, but small balanced subsets change unweighted precision and F1.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: Algebraic Integer Quantization for Machine Learning Applications
stories.summary: In this article, we propose algebraic integer number formats (AINF) as a framework for highly configurable and accurate compressed computation.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: TabMF: Learning Dataset Representations with Tabular Foundation Models
stories.summary: Representations of supervised datasets support higher-level machine-learning tasks such as dataset retrieval and distribution-shift monitoring.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: DRYLAB-Bench: Benchmarking the Biosecurity Risk of Agentic LLM Mutation Design
stories.summary: As large language models (LLMs) acquire advanced biological design capabilities, they offer substantial research benefits but simultaneously introduce severe dual-use risks, such as engineering enhanced pathogens or drug-resistant bacteria.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
stories.summary: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: Travel Back To Move Forward: Retrospective Exploration and Evolving for Long Horizon Agents
stories.summary: Large language model agents increasingly operate in long-horizon environments where early mistakes can trigger cascading failures and trap agents in dead-end trajectories.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: Can Failed Trajectories Reveal Where Agents Go Wrong? Agentic Failure Attribution Without Step-Level Labels
stories.summary: Failure attribution for LLM agents aims to identify decisive steps responsible for task failure, which is critical for debugging and improving agentic systems.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: RARA: Robust Policy Fine-Tuning through Retrieval-Anchored Representation Alignment for Robotic Manipulation
stories.summary: Pre-trained robot policies, such as Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, provide a strong foundation for generalist robotic manipulation, but adapting them to new tasks with only a few demonstrations remains challenging.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: Forward Dynamics Models
stories.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models and world action models (WAMs) have advanced robotic policy learning by building on pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) and video generative models (VGMs), respectively.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training
stories.summary: Large language models have achieved remarkable advances in complex reasoning. However, scaling reasoning post-training with ever-larger corpora can substantially increase training cost without proportional performance gains.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: Tabular Foundation Models Are Effectively Shallow
stories.summary: In-context-learning Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) are uniquely suited to scenarios with limited resources or privacy constraints, as they solve new tasks without additional training.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: MathVis: Can AI Reason through Drawing? A Benchmark for Mathematical Figure Generation
stories.summary: This paper introduces MathVis, a benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to visualize frontier mathematical problems and perform diagram-assisted reasoning.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
stories.summary: As AI agents increasingly rely on external tools, accurate retrieval is essential for reliable behavior. Existing methods optimize semantic relevance but largely ignore tool availability during execution.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: Your Discrete Graph Diffusion Model is Secretly Memorizing
stories.summary: Discrete graph diffusion models (GDMs) corrupt the graph structure by adding noise independently to nodes and edges under a Markovian noise model.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.

stories.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
stories.summary: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited.
stories.whyItMatters: arXiv paper, first version published Oct 12, 2026.
